title: Life-cycle fund, or NPS?
intro: Two glide paths, two different jobs. File each trait with the wrapper it belongs to.

cards.text: Point it at any dated goal — a 2036 education corpus, a 2046 house
Redeemable any time once the 3/2/1% exit-load window passes
The target year is in the scheme's name; max six per fund house
SEBI glide bands; near maturity only AA+ debt maturing before target
Tier I money locked for 15 years or until age 60
Up to 60% of the corpus withdrawable tax-free on completion
Auto Choice has trimmed equity with age for years
Built primarily for retirement; joining is voluntary, adoption thin

debrief: Both automate the same glide logic — equity falling as the date nears — but the wrappers differ in purpose. The NPS trades liquidity for a tax break: locked to retirement, rewarded on exit. The life-cycle fund trades the tax break for freedom: any dated goal, exit-loads instead of locks, ordinary fund taxation. The issue's conclusion is the useful one: they overlap but do different jobs, and can sit side by side in one plan — NPS for retirement's tax edge, life-cycle funds for every other dated goal.
